biomarker_value.notes: The paper identifies biomarkers qualitatively (which genera/functions are biomarkers) but does not report specific numerical values for individual biomarkers in text. Values are shown in figures but not quantified in the narrative.

value: Study population: 15 semi-isolated Yanomami individuals from Brazil
Comparative groups: Yanomami from Venezuela (n=8), Matses from Peru (n=24), Tunapuco from Andes (n=12), US urban population (n=44)
Sequencing method: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing on HiSeq 2500
Total reads generated: ~219 million reads (~14 million per sample)
Taxonomic classification: Kraken using NCBI bacterial and archaeal genomes
Functional classification: SUPER-FOCUS using SEED database gene families
Statistical tests: Kruskal-Wallis (alpha=0.05), LDA score >4.0, Wilcoxon test, PERMANOVA (999 permutations)
Ethical approvals: Oswaldo Cruz Foundation Ethics Committee No. 638/11, CONEP No. 16907
Key finding: Yanomami/Brazil showed unique functional features including higher abundance of regulation/cell signaling, motility/chemotaxis, and virulence genes
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: Based on shotgun metagenomic data, we characterized the gut microbiome of the Yanomami from Brazil and compared taxonomically and functionally with the Yanomami from Venezuela, with other traditional groups from the Amazon and an urban-industrialized group.
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive metadata about study design, populations, methods, and key findings.

host_species.evidence_quote: Participants were requested to provide a morning fecal sample
host_species.section: Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection
host_species.notes: The study examines human gut microbiome in Yanomami and other human populations. Species is inferred from the human study context.
